newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Light asked to delay Black Point.
newsitem.headline: China Light asked to delay Black Point.

text.p: China Light and Power Co Ltd faces slower earnings growth in the coming five years following a Hong Kong government request that the company delay the construction of its newest power plant, stock analysts said on Tuesday.
The company's earnings growth is tied to the growth in its fixed assets as detailed under a scheme of control worked out between the company and the government.
Analysts said on Tuesday that an independent group commissioned by the government had concluded that Hong Kong would not require generating capacity to be provided by China Light's Black Point plant.

China Light and Power has three months to put forward its own arguments for the need for Black Point, the South China Morning Post said. China Light officials were not immediately available for comment.
"It's tough to argue the need for the plant. We are at the bottom of the (electricity) demand cycle," said James Ng, research analyst at MeesPierson Securities.

Black Point, which will have a total of eight generators, has been delayed several times in the past. Analysts said the delay in the construction of the remainder of the plant will mean low growth in the company's assets.
"The company needs to spend in order to grow its assets," said Rohan Dalziell, analyst at ING Barings.
China Light shares were down HK$1.10 at HK$33.90 in Tuesday morning trade.
